works.depth_reason: Single decision (when to fire while continuously aimed); shots/hits are tracked but only feed an end-of-round accuracy readout, never a later decision.

works.novelty_reason: Reuses seed-001's instant aim-and-fire hit-test verbatim, adding one real rule: a second target type (packet) that penalizes on hit and resets the combo, forcing target discrimination absent from seed-001.
works.depth_reason: Two decisions (aim position, then fire-or-hold based on the reticle-highlighted target's type); combo/mult is a score multiplier only, not state that changes what is required next.

works.novelty_reason: No predecessor (seed-001, seed-002) judges a target's own internal timer; both resolve on-press instantly. Introduces hold-drag-then-release-timed-against-a-shrinking-ring, changing the decision from spatial aim to temporal release-timing.
works.depth_reason: Two interacting decisions (where to hold + when to release, judged against CORE_START/CORE_END of the flare's shrink); up to 2 concurrent flares force prioritization, but no state persists beyond score/streak.

works.novelty_reason: Reuses seed-003's judge-target's-own-timer principle (BAND_START/BAND_END mirrors seed-003's CORE_START/CORE_END) but reverts to an instant tap and adds a third graded outcome (TOO EARLY vs STRAINED) on a fixed multi-slot grid — one real modification, not a new judging principle.
works.depth_reason: Two decisions (which slot + timing against its energy band); up to 3 concurrent veins force prioritization, matching seed-003's structure with no additional non-score state.

works.novelty_reason: Reuses the judge-target's-own-timer principle from seed-003/seed-004 (PEAK_THRESHOLD on emberBrightness) but changes it from a one-shot life-arc to a repeating sine pulse the player can wait through, plus a player-side swing cooldown — one real modification, not a new principle.
works.depth_reason: Two decisions (net position via physics-based movement + when to spend the cooldown-gated swing) across up to 5 embers; streak/multiplier is a score multiplier only, as in seed-002/seed-003/seed-004.

works.novelty_reason: No predecessor (seed-001..seed-005) fires a traveling projectile; all resolve on-press instantly against whatever is at the aim point now. Introduces angle-based aiming with real flight time and multi-target pierce, changing the decision from 'is a target here now' to 'what line will intersect several moving targets' future paths'.
works.depth_reason: Aim-angle and fire-timing interact with wisps' independent velocities (lead-prediction) and with each other via hitSet/splice: a wisp claimed mid-flight by one harpoon is removed from the pool for any other simultaneously-flying harpoon, an emergent interaction the on-screen text never states.

works.novelty_reason: No predecessor lets the player invest a chosen hold-duration for more power; seed-001..seed-006 all use fixed-duration cooldowns after acting, never a charge-before-acting resource. Changes the decision from targeting/timing precision to a time-investment trade-off against multiple falling threats.
works.depth_reason: Position and charge-duration decisions interact with meteors' own mutable state: an under-powered hit permanently downgrades m.type (L to M to S), a real non-score state change that alters what a later shot on that same meteor requires.

works.novelty_reason: No predecessor (seed-001..007) has a resource that persists and accumulates across multiple target hits to gate a second, higher-value target type; seed-007's charge is the closest analogue but is per-shot and resets on release, while VOLT CACHE's currency is banked from cell hits and spent (or denied) on vault hits across the whole round, changing the decision from per-target timing/aim to cross-target resource sequencing.
works.depth_reason: Two interacting decisions (which target to hit, and implicit sequencing of cells before vaults) with real non-score state (currency, incremented by cell hits and consumed or denied by vault hits); the currency-gate interaction is stated directly in the title-screen text, so no emergent behavior beyond what the rules state.

works.novelty_reason: No predecessor (seed-001..008) binds a sustained hold to one specific target instance; seed-007's hold-to-charge is untargeted and never cancels on re-aim, seed-003's hold-drag-release only resolves against whichever flare is nearest at release, and seed-008 has no hold at all (both its target kinds resolve on instant click) — TETHER LOCK is the first work where holding accumulates progress against one committed target and re-aiming onto a different target discards that progress entirely, changing the decision from timing/aim precision or resource sequencing to sustained single-target commitment with a real switching cost.
works.depth_reason: Two interacting decisions (which target to commit to, and whether to keep holding as its own life timer runs or abandon for a safer one) with real non-score state (holdProgress, which persists only while locked to one target id and is discarded on switch, release, or the held target's own expiry); the switch-cancels-progress rule is stated directly in the title-screen text, so no emergent behavior beyond what the rules state.
